guarantees.claim: On reset (rst_ni = 0), break_st_q is forced to BRK_CHK.
In BRK_CHK state, if event_rx_break_err is asserted, next state becomes BRK_WAIT; otherwise break_st_q remains BRK_CHK.
In BRK_WAIT state, if rx_in is high, next state becomes BRK_CHK; otherwise break_st_q remains BRK_WAIT.
If break_st_q takes any value besides BRK_CHK or BRK_WAIT (illegal state), next state is forced to BRK_CHK.

assumptions.claim: The external UART RX line (rx_in) is expected to eventually return to idle (high) after a break condition; otherwise break_st_q remains in BRK_WAIT blocking further break detection.
assumptions.risk: If rx_in stays low permanently (e.g., line stuck), break_st_q will never leave BRK_WAIT, preventing detection of subsequent break events and possibly affecting protocol recovery.

uncertain_points.claim: BRK_WAIT state has no timeout mechanism. If rx_in remains low indefinitely, break_st_q will never recover, and no error is signaled.
uncertain_points.cond: break_st_q == BRK_WAIT and rx_in == 0 for an unbounded time
uncertain_points.risk: Break detection becomes permanently stalled, hiding line faults and preventing re-detection of break events. This may violate protocol expectations if the UART is used for error/special-condition signaling.

uncertain_points.claim: The default clause silently forces recovery to BRK_CHK without any error signal. An illegal state might indicate a transient fault (e.g., a bit-flip), but this is not recorded or escalated.
uncertain_points.risk: Soft errors in the state register would be masked, possibly hiding a persistent fault or corruption that could affect later break handling.
